title: Preserve OAS shrinkage when constant asset offsets dominate scale
observation: Adding a constant 1e150 value to a zero-variance asset changes OAS covariance from diag(2,3) to diag(2.5,2.5) in the existing v2 implementation.
cause: Normalization by uncentered absolute levels lets an irrelevant constant asset erase the quartic dispersion terms used for shrinkage intensity.
severity: incorrect arithmetic, state or evidence admission on valid/ambiguous boundary inputs
implemented_change: Subtract a per-asset reference before selecting the common scale, with a normalized fallback for genuinely overflowing differences. Preserve explicit rejection of unrepresentable final covariance.
predicted_consequence: New constructed regressions fail on the recorded parent and pass after the repair while the existing bounded suite passes.
